correctness.rationale: Every finite bipartite chain graph with named sides A,B is representable as a creation word, 0 inserting an isolated A vertex, 1 inserting a B vertex joined to all preceding A; nested B neighborhoods give the word order, including empty structures. The rank-three Hintikka/Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé invariant H(G) is built from realized atomic triple types and their extension sets. It is a COMPLETE invariant of rank≤3 sentences (not just a heuristic colour refinement): one-round tuple-type recursion induces exact 3-type of the empty tuple. Appending either creation letter preserves 3-equivalence by an EF strategy matching new vertices and using the winning old strategy. Thus closure of quotient word states is an infinite completeness certificate. Independently RECOMPUTED H for every one of the actual 2833 source certificate words, checked all signatures unique, all 5666 claimed successors exactly, BFS reachability of all 2833 states and distances equal claimed shortest word lengths. The maximum is 21 with exactly two words at that distance: 001100110011011001100, 110011001001100110011. This is exhaustive for all creation words because the fully verified transition table is closed, not a bounded word-sample extrapolation.
residual_risks: Rank 3 is ordinary first-order quantifier nesting depth in the named-side graph signature; no unlabelled or ordered signature extension follows.
Closure follows from the separately reconstructed EF append congruence; raw certificate alone could not establish the all-size conclusion.
